1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is produced by the expression of a polynucleotide encoding the at least one BMC polypeptide in a host cell.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme that catalyzes a specific biochemical reaction.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes that catalyze different biochemical reactions.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides, wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons, wherein the different BMC operons are derived from different bacterial species.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide, wherein the method is performed to enhance the metabolic capabilities of the host cell.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product, wherein the product is a bioactive product. 

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments, wherein the compartments are engineered for specific metabolic functions.
